Turathi Blue by Afnan is a Aromatic Aquatic fragrance for men. Turathi Blue was launched in 2021. The nose behind this fragrance is Imran Fazlani. Top note is Citruses; middle notes are Amber and Woodsy Notes; base notes are Musk, Spices and Patchouli.

hitch117 12/09/25 21:53

First, gentlemen, many of you are misusing two very important fragrance terms, "maceration" and "maturation." While similar, they are not the same. MaCERation occurs in a vessel in the perfume house and is part of the formulation process. And, like wine, maTURation occurs in the bottle and is accelerated when some oxygen enters the headspace to displace the juice sprayed. Thus endeth the lesson. Onto the review.

I can think of a thousand things I'd rather do with $500US than purchase a bottle of Bvlgari Tygar, but... I wanted to experience something similar to that legendary OG fragrance so I purchased Afnan Turathi Blue blind. As with many Middle Eastern fragrances, Turathi Blue was a little rough out of the box. But the first wearing, even in its immature infancy, was absolutely intoxicating. After a few minutes the sharp edges softened, and as it dried down it became a luscious, beautiful, uplifting experience while still remaining appropriately masculine.

Every time I wear it, it becomes even smoother and more compelling. The opening is now even more delightful than the drydown. And it just keeps getting better! It's winter here now and I can't wait to smell it again next spring after it comes out of hibernation and has matured even more. (Oh, WTF, writing this has me pining for it so I went and took a couple of hits, LOL.)

According to acquaintances and my own observations retracing my paths in the hallways, the sillage is impressive. Longevity could be longer, but that just delays the opportunity to re-spray and enjoy once again that wonderful citrus opening.

I like it so much I've purchased two additional bottles. When I estimate that I've got a couple months left in the first, I'll break out bottle #2 and wear it a couple of times then put it away to grow-up some while I finish bottle #1. Ohmygoodness I love this fragrance. Here's hoping you do as well.

I went a little nuts and purchased several other Tygar inspirations: Rue Broca Théorème Homme, Maison Alhambra Sceptre Bronzite, and Lattafa Al Qiam Silver. All three are really good, but I still prefer the Turathi Blue. I also have a bottle of Paris Corner North Stag Expressions I Un on the way. Sooner or later I'll get around to reviewing those and I'll edit this review should the latter turn out to be a superior offering.

My excellent experience with Turathi Blue was SO positive that I purchased the masculine-leaning Turathi Brown and the unisex Turathi Electric. The Turathi Brown is every bit as wonderful as the Turathi Blue and will sustain me through the colder months. I've already penned a glowing review here on that one. The jury is still out on the Turathi Electric. I'm not quite sure I understand that one yet. I'll try it one again come warmer weather and see how that one matures. It may be as simple as... as a old-school gentleman I just prefer the masculine over the unisex.

ProfoundlySoy 12/03/25 19:22

Mine has been sitting in a dark cupboard for a year and i’ve come around a bit to how it smells– totally different from when I first got it. It was genuinely pretty bad when I first opened it last christmas, it smelled like bug spray with some strange spice mix.

Bug spray smell is gone 13 months later. Now it’s got a more bright uplifting grapefruit smelling opening reminiscent (but absolutely not the same) as BDC EDP, accompanied by sweet ginger ale. You really want to like musk to like this because you’re getting it by the bucketload.

There is a story around this gem of a perfume.
I used to not trust word of mouth while buying perfumes. Used to think that perfume reviewers and youtubers are not trustworthy, and rarely bought what was recommended by many people. Also don't know why I used to end up buying some clone of a remotely known designer/niche perfume and I ended up having many "not so nice" perfumes. But then when I finally got this and smelled it for the first time, it blew my mind and gave me some kind of good thought to think. I realised why people regarded this so high. I still remember the first day of smelling this gem, and I was surprised by how amazing it smelled, and what I had been missing for 3 years. Realised that I need to trust word of mouth on Youtube. From this perfume onwards I started buying the right perfumes and now my collection of affordable perfumes looks promising.
Afnan Turathi Blue is one of my top 5-6 favourites. Just sometimes I feel that the perfume is not that long lasting maybe olfactory fatigue, who knows.
Afnan, thanks!! you are amazing for democratizing this luxury.

cbarology 10/16/25 06:55

The "clone" that made me a believer in "masturbation" er.... "maturation" or "maceration". Whatever you call it. Anyway, this is definitely one of those fragrances that you need to spray a few times after unboxing, then leave in a dark room for like a month or 2.

The first week with this, I hated it. I smelled the grapefruit fizz which was my favorite part about it, but then going out in the sun and sweating made it start to smell like weird, musky body odor. No joke. It was nasty. I thought to myself "this is supposed to be a WARM WEATHER fragrance? If so, why tf do i smell like b.o. and piss when the heat hits my skin?". Welp, that's changed after 2 or so months. Now you have to really like citrus - grapefruit in particular - to like this. The grapefruit soda/fizz scent is Turathi Blue's most prominent note, and it is a beautiful grapefruit fizz. You get a bit of light musk and woods on the drydown, but that grapefruit wins it over. Turathi Blue also performs like a beast. 4-5 sprays and I'm set for 8+hrs in the Philippines heat. If you get it on your clothes, prepare to have it still smelling like Turathi Blue after a wash.

For how inexpensive this is, I think it's worth the pick up for warmer weather. Just take note that this ACTUALLY needs "masturbation". You're probably not going to like it out of the box. Wear your more expensive frags for hot weather in the meantime.

That grapefruit in the opening works wonders in the heat and you could layer this scent over the top of other blue fragrances that last longer and have a bit more depth to them like Bleu De Chanel EDP (or Parfum). I've also layered this with Ralph Lauren Polo 67 EDP, and the pineapple note in that frag blends so well with the grapefruit in Turathi Blue. Layering will also help with the performance and longevity, as unfortunately on its own I only get between 4 - 6 hours of this before it's barely detectable on the skin.

For the price this one offers great bang for your buck value, if it lasted a little longer that would have put this up there with one of the best value for money men's fragrances on the market today. For the price of around $30 USD, over spray to your hearts content. An absolute banger

alexandrewb 08/24/25 20:10

Turathi Blue by Afnan is a men's fragrance that combines freshness and intensity in a balanced way, while being both versatile and striking.

Top notes, citrus, open the fragrance vibrantly and invigoratingly, bringing an immediate sensation of freshness.
Heart notes: spices, patchouli, and woody nuances add depth, sophistication, and a more robust, masculine touch.
Base notes: amber and musk, responsible for the warm, sensual, and enveloping tone, ensuring density and longevity.

The result is a citrus-woody fragrance with oriental touches, which manages to be both fresh and intense, ideal for those seeking projection and personality.

Longevity: around 7 hours on the skin, sometimes longer depending on the climate and skin tone.
Strong projection in the first 2 hours, then becomes closer to the skin, but still noticeable.
A striking trail, it leaves an elegant trail without being invasive.

It works well for everyday use in professional and social settings during the day, thanks to its citrusy freshness. The amber and musky base ensures presence, making it great for dates, dinners, or casual evenings out.
Weather: Best suited for spring and summer, but can also be worn in fall. In harsh winters, it may lack weight compared to heavier perfumes.

Turathi Blue is perfect for the modern man who likes to exude elegance and confidence without overdoing it. It balances the fresh and woody sides well, making it a versatile fragrance for a variety of situations.

Final Score: 09/10

A versatile, elegant, and excellent value fragrance, standing out for its solid performance and balance between citrus freshness and oriental depth.

The Turathi opens up at the opening with alcohol and general citrus notes. The opening needed about a minute to settle on my skin before I started to get a grapefruit closer to Tygar. For the opening, think of the Tygar opening with less sweetness. After about five minutes, I began to pick up ambery wood notes that differently added a richer and needed depth to the opening. Eventually, at about the hour mark, you can pick up some strong musk along with the ambroxan that is so prominent in Tygar. While all the notes are similar to the original, you pick up more of the musk in the Turathi, and the ambroxan was not as overpowered over all the other notes as it is in the original at the dry down.

As for its performance, Turathi Blue creates a delightful arms-length bubble around you during the opening and middle stages. When the drydown kicks in, the projection narrows to less than a foot for the next four hours before settling into a subtle skin scent. In total, you can expect this fresh fragrance to linger for around six hours, which is quite respectable for its category.

Overall, Turathi is a great dupe that is exceptionally close to the original. Other than a slightly more synthetic opening and being more musky in the middle, they got it about 90% close. This similarity is quite exciting, especially considering the price of Tygar. But if you can afford Tygar, go for it and support the art of perfumery.

I told Myself I wouldn't blind buy another fragrance but I wanted a cheapie that I could use whenever, wherever.

I had heard a lot about the Turathi Blue hype, so I gave in and bought it.

It arrived yesterday, and so far (pre maceration) I have no regrets. I think I got what I paid for.

The opening is a sharp, sweet candied grapefruit, which I wasn't really expecting but have no issues with. Turathi blue quickly becomes less sweet and more woody and musky as it dries down. I think the note pyramid is very accurate to how this smells.

It smells fine on skin, but in the air is where it shines. It's nothing totally unique, but it does smell damn good. The dry down is a familiar and simple scent profile- a "blue" shower gel scent, somewhat in the same realm as Versace Dylan Blue and Bleu de Chanel (I am not saying they smell the same).

As for the comparisons to Tygar from Bvlgari, I can't say its a "dupe" because I have never smelled it.

The performance straight out of the box is also decent. A moderate 5-6 hours of longevity and moderate sillage.

Overall, this is good. Definitley worth the money. Pretty simple, almost boring- but sometimes a simple scent is necessary. I am glad I picked this one up (so Far).

7.5/10

AFNAN TURATHI BLUE (ATB) is BRIGHT YET DARK, a CITRIC-SPICY 'BLEU' FRESHIE W/ SOME DEPTH & DEVELOPMENT (ATB smells like a rindy slightly fresher version of BdC Parfum like BdC Parfum Summer, ATB is darker than BdC EdT & EdP; also, similar to Rochas L'Homme (RL) just replace the juniper in RL w/ grapefruit but ATB is not as bright unisex as RL)

Opening: is fresh-sharp-rindy-zesty-citrus, trendy fresh citrus & spice combo, spice deriving from the zesty-citrus + amber-wood (of the fuzzy variety)

more rindy not fruity/sweet grapefruit, the grapefruit is detectable but not extreme, if it were overdone Turathi Blue (ATB) would be too funky-rindy-sour, just the right amount of rindy/tart/sharp/freshness that's lightly sweet mixed with fuzzy ambroxan + amberwood w/ slight aquatic-'bleu'ness + slightly soapy

Full-dry: a little creaminess (probably the musk) is added to the scent composition as the bleu/blue subsides some and the soapiness is slightly shampoo(ish), and the patchouli gets more detectable;

Great fragrance composition (especially @ the price point, if you told me Alberto Morillas or Jacques Cavallier was the perfumer I'd believe you); has an aire/sophisticated/classy vibe but it's a little earthy too (may not be palatable for sensitive noises); Versatile, can be worn vacation, work/business, or gym; any age could wear ATB but I would not call it 'youthful';


Sillage'/Projection: GOOD, especially 1-2 hrs in then has an in-close scent bubble but still get whiffs from breeze

Performance/Longevity: GREAT, last 12+ hours on clothes (so probably about half that on skin)


I see why all the youtube hype, it's deserved, for once (some of them youtubers be hyping boo boo frags)

Pretty sure this is going to be another unjustified hyped frag that I’ll be moving on, will give it another couple of wears before I write it off, but first impressions are just not doing it for me.

Update: Well guess what it’s still garbage, the imaginary maceration everyone bangs on about has done zilch (oh what a surprise) & to think we listen to these people to find out if a frag is worthy or not, every-time I read something like “I left this & came back to it a week later & it was completely different & amazing” I laugh my head off, honestly people believe any bullshit! 💩

Most Popular Positive Reviews

heylegros 11/08/22 09:50

I bought a bottle of Turathi Blue out of pure curiosity. It's dirt cheap, people said this was a clone of Bvlgari Tygar, so what's not to like?

Well, I would agree that this is somewhat similar to Tygar in the opening, but this is not nearly as good. Don't get me wrong, this isn't bad either. Just don't expect a $400 fragrance for barely a tenth of the price.

Turathi Blue's opening is very citrusy, but unlike Tygar, it's not "grapefruit" citrusy specifically. It's a pleasant opening without a doubt, very "blueish", very fresh and quite invigorating. Pretty good stuff, although somewhat synthetic. But again, Tygar isn't much of a natural-smelling fragrance anyway; its strength truly lies in delivering a phenomenally simple yet well-rounded masterclass in masculine elegance oozing with confidence, which is very linear but incredibly potent. Turathi Blue is good, but being well-rounded just isn't one of its outstanding qualities.

As it dries down, Turathi Blue's woody notes arise alongside the citruses, a backbone consisting of musk and amber also surfaces, which brings Turathi Blue closer to a Bleu de Chanel EDT than a Bvlgari Tygar. But the woods and amber are not as prominent...this remains a citrus-driven scent. It does feel quite synthetic in the dry down, so be warned. It's much more pleasant to catch a whiff of this in the air than it is to smell it up close on the skin.

Mid-through the dry down, it becomes a tad spicy, and those reviewers who talked about a cumin note are most definitely referring to that stage of the scent. I know what they mean by what seems like a hint of cumin/sweat, but that is not quite what I pick up. This likely stems from an awkward mix of those spicy notes and the synthetic aspect of the scent, which again is not nearly as dramatic when smelled from a distance rather than up close on the skin. I do have to say that I would have preferred that those spicy notes be toned down just a notch. But overall this is really pleasant throughout, and definitely a really good blue scent for the price. I'd wear this over Bleu de Chanel EDT on any day. It smells better and lasts longer.

I was quite surprised to discover how well this performs. This lasts for several hours and projects quite impressively. At that price point, again it's difficult not to be pleased with Afnan's ability to deliver such an overall good-smelling product with such longevity, especially when so many high profile designers fail to make their freshies and blue scents nearly as long-lasting as this.

In a few words: A cheapie that's kind of a cross between Bleu de Chanel EDT and Bvlgari Tygar, but more citrusy than Bleu EDT, and not nearly as well-rounded as Tygar.
Pros: Excellent value for the price. Solid performance. Pleasant blue scent throughout.
Cons: Synthetic when smelled from up close. Spicy notes could have been toned down a notch.
Overall rating (out of five stars): ★★★

Colonel Stanley 12/05/24 23:57

This is my second Turathi. Batch - 07 / 24.

One of our regular reviewers has already written about it, so let's start with this - Tygar is not a unique perfume that should be cloned (!)... but if the market demands it, it's natural that such fragrances will eventually appear.

Turathi, Theoreme, Al Qiam Silver, Bronzite, JL Immortal... Afnan Turathi costs the same as Lattafa and Maison Alhambra, they are about $3 - 5 more expensive than Rue Broca. They all smell the same, slightly synthetic, without exception... but among them, Turathi is, in my opinion, the least offensive, it is the most wearable, nice and has the best parameters. Parameters are little better than Lattafa, little better than Afnan's sub-brand Rue Broca (but this one is very close...) and much more better than the other rivals. The slightly synthetic opening is definitely less synthetic than in many other popular Arabic citrus perfumes. After a few months, this opening will smooth out anyway. I like the smell of citrus, but this smells more like a lemonade, citrus sparkling drink....which is nice for me. That's why it's peaceful and no one will accuse you of having bad taste. Just an idea for the summer. It's a little sweet and it's slightly sour, 2 in 1. I am very glad that this is not the full interpretation of the grapefruit scent that our friends from the UAE can offer us. I definitely prefer this way out of this difficult situation than the terribly artificial, harsh opening that we encounter in many other cases. So I appreciate Afnan's interpretation. It's also not the most natural, but at least no one convinces us from the very beginning that what we smell is a real grapefruit or other citrus. And I appreciate it. Lemonade, very pleasant... that's it. This is a very clever solution to the problem. As I have already written, this is not a clone, let's treat it as a different scent, a different proposition. It's just some inspiration, your own idea and the resulting savings, as shown by the price. "Citruses" are rather delicate and stay with us until the very end. When we get to the base notes, then... mainly sweet amber and some woody notes, but also musk/ambroxan and patchouli complement each other nicely and the light citrus note is beautifuly wrapped in them. I didn't find any harsh spices. Summa summarum, the scent itself is pleasantly surprising, it's not Bulgari and rather not very similar to BdC. Typical summer scent, but it's not a clone. Delicate but with good projection. We feel fresh and at ease, nothing about this frag really bothers us. The beach, a walk on the promenade, one little drink in a restaurant by the sea. I will write even more - you can use it
at work or during less formal meetings, it will not offend anyone. As is the case with many other Arabic perfumes, this time you should remember that -

1. Let's subject it to so called "home maceration" for a period of 4 - 8 months... so it's best to buy it in November. It will be good enough in May or June. This is just common sense planning for perfumes from the UAE. We pay so little and then, after 10 - 15 sprays our frags just mature in the cupboard, that's all. It's not a great feat, but the results can be very surprising. We can do the same with autumn and winter fragrances... let's buy them in February or March and wait until October. It's simple, pure savings.

2. In the case of Turathi, after spraying, wait 5-10 minutes until the scent becomes more refined and then present it to the whole world. 😉 These are one of the least synthetic Arabic summer perfumes... they are no more artificial than many other, much more expensive similar fragrances from well-known brands... so there is nothing to be ashamed of.

3. If You live in moderate climate, Afnan will be great from early June to mid-September.

That's all. Good Luck. 👍

Got a few wearings out of this

This does stay citrussy and juicy all the way, even though woody and sweet aspects come out more into the dry-down.

Fragrances tend to last more than average on me, but this is one that stays till I wash it off. Projection is very good for up to 4h on me.

Great scent IMO!
